claims.text: The initial eutectic high-entropy alloy microstructure consists of dual-phase lamellar colonies.
The lamellar colonies contain numerous internal boundaries.
Optimizing lamellar colony size can reduce microcracking during room-temperature tensile deformation.
Optimizing lamellar colony orientation can reduce microcracking during room-temperature tensile deformation.
Optimizing lamellar colony size and orientation can promote more homogeneous deformation.
Reducing microcracking and promoting more homogeneous deformation can increase tensile strength relative to an unmodified lamellar-colony baseline.
Reducing microcracking and promoting more homogeneous deformation can increase room-temperature tensile ductility relative to an unmodified lamellar-colony baseline.
The proposed intervention is applicable only to eutectic high-entropy alloys with dual-phase lamellar colonies.
The exact relationship between lamellar colony size, colony orientation, and mechanical properties is uncertain.
